To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) gi is not a constant, but varies among species and within species, (2) gi does not scale with biochemical capacity for photosynthetic carbon gain, (3) gi does not necessarily increase with photosynthetic rate, (4) gi is a key component of WUE, PNUE and delta, (5) variation in gi adds to the variation in delta, and (6) variation in gi may be a key factor in explaining the evolution of photosynthetic traits

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
gi does not scale with the biochemical capacity of photosynthesis, and that the relationship between gi and gs varies among species and with environment.

there is no simple and explicit scaling between photosynthesis and gi and that this has important implications for our understanding of the relationships between photosynthetic capacity and WUE, N use, and delta.
gi does not scale perfectly or proportionally with photosynthesis, and that this variation in gi is an important determinant of variation in PNUE, WUE, and delta.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is no single, universal, predictable, and explicit pattern among species, genera and life forms in gi, in the draw-down from Ci-to-Cc, in the gi- photosynthesis relationship, or in delta.
the economics of water use in photosynthesis (A/WUE and delta) are not predictable from gs alone.
there is a great deal of variation among species in the relationship of gi to A and that this variation is a major source of variation in PNUE and WUE and in delta.
The main takeaway from our work is that
gi is an important determinant of photosynthetic water and nitrogen use efficiency and carbon isotope discrimination, but that it is not a constant fraction of gs.
gi must be considered explicitly in any effort to scale photosynthetic capacity, WUE, and delta.
the internal conductance for CO2 does not scale with the biochemical capacity of photosynthesis and thus cannot be assumed to be infinite.
